speaker: Doctor
text: I see you experienced a difficult delivery with an 11-pound baby; I have requested a CT of your abdomen and pelvis to look for complications like a uterine infection or appendicitis, and a urinalysis to rule out a urinary tract infection. While we await those results, can you tell me if you have any nausea, vomiting, or visible abdominal guarding?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Uterine tenderness. I also have Decreased bowel sounds, Increased frequency of urination, Fever.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Postpartum Endometritis with potential associated urinary tract involvement.

The combination of fever, uterine tenderness, and a history of prolonged labor and macrosomia strongly suggests endometritis. The decreased bowel sounds may indicate a developing ileus, while the increased urination frequency suggests a concurrent urinary tract infection or bladder distension. I will now await your final confirmation regarding nausea or vomiting to complete the assessment before proceeding with definitive management.
